eli: Heads-up: follow-up from the RFC — operator wants a deterministic way to promote a regional replica to primary without exposing users to duplicate-appends or split-brain. Can we agree on the fence-and-verify pattern?
tara: Fence-and-verify sounds right. We should define what "fence" means operationally: deny writes on old primary, rotate lease token, and ensure no stray active workers accept traffic.
omar: +1. My worry is race between operator action and client retries hitting an old egress. We need an egress-level lease TTL check so proxies reject writes if the cluster lease is stale.
eli: Proposal outline: 1) Acquire global promotion lock in control-plane (lease K), 2) instruct old-primary to refuse new writes and emit final watermark, 3) replicate/confirm in-flight idempotency records + last-seq, 4) run integrity validators on sample keys, 5) flip pointer, 6) release lock.
tara: For step 3, do we stream the in-flight dedupe metadata or snapshot it? Snapshotting may be simpler for correctness at cost of latency. Streaming is lower-latency but complex.
omar: Snapshot is simpler and safer for first rollout. Implementation: on fence, pause acceptors, flush idempotency map to control-plane store, ack back when persisted.
opsbot: NOTE: promotion dry-run schedule request received. Use runbook: https://go.redwood/runbooks/region-promotion-template
eli: Good. We should also pre-announce to customers with residency constraints: exporting dedupe metadata may contain small PII (client-provided idempotency keys) — need to ensure we treat as metadata, encrypt at rest and in-flight.
tara: Legal needs a short blurb: metadata persisted transiently for promotion window only. Add automatic purge policy: TTL 72h post-promote. For Private deployments, require customer-managed KMS by default.
omar: On verification (step 4), let's implement a 'compare sample' job: pick N tenant keys (configurable), compare versions between source and target region after snapshot applied. Fail if mismatch. This prevents odd reordering.
eli: Also propose adding a promotion-mode metric 'promote_inflight_replays' counting writes that were replayed during promotion so we can assess risk.
omar: We should implement write fencing tokens: clients and edge proxies must present a region-lease-token signed by control-plane for writes. Old tokens become invalid after fence. Proxies should fetch new token post-reconcile.
tara: That's a lot of plumbing. For quick rollout we can rely on operator-driven fencing + snapshot + disable-old-writes. Longer term add token-based egress.
eli: Agreed. Roadmap: Phase 0 (safe rollback): operator-fence + snapshot + validate-sample + flip pointer + TTLed metadata + advisory. Phase 1: egress-lease-token + client SDK changes + metrics. Phase 2: streaming idempotency with per-tenant flow-control.
omar: Edge case: network partition where both regions think they hold lease. Add extra safety: control-plane lease must be stored in a highly-available quorum that operators cannot override without explicit --force flag and justification.
opsbot: SECURITY REMINDER: any cross-region transfer must be logged to audit stream. Auditors notified for tenant X promotions for first 30 days.
tara: Operator checklist draft (short):
```
- Acquire promotion lock (control-plane)
- Put shadow region into drain (stop accepts)
- Wait for snapshot ack from shadow
- Run sample-compare job (pass/fail)
- If pass: flip routing pointer, enable writes
- Monitor promote_inflight_replays, write-errors, client-err-rate for 60m
- If anomalies: immediately revert pointer and open incident
```
omar: Nice. Also include quick rollback command examples in runbook and log snippets operators should look for.
eli: Communication notes: update status page if promotion may affect SLA; short advisory in tenant dashboard; recommended app patterns: client-provided idempotency-key + exponential backoff on retry.
tara: One more thing: for GDPR/data residency customers, we must ensure the snapshot excludes payloads and only contains idempotency keys + sequence numbers. No full user content is shipped. Add verification tests to assert stripped snapshots contain no user content.
omar: Implementation owners: infra-runtime owns snapshot export + persist, eng-platform owns control-plane lock and metrics, docs owns runbook and tenant advisory. I'll file ownership tickets.
eli: I'll coordinate a dry-run next week with ops and legal. Tagging: @tara @omar — pls review the operator checklist PR when it's ready.
opsbot: Promotion dry-run created: DR-2024-11-06-01. Notifications scheduled.
